designationHistory.name: Caloosahatchee Reservation
designationHistory.indexText: President Woodrow Wilson established the Caloosahatchee Reservation by Executive Order 3299; it is now Caloosahatchee National Wildlife Refuge.

sources.name: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service: Caloosahatchee National Wildlife Refuge, About Us
USFWS, Pine Island, Matlacha Pass, Island Bay and Caloosahatchee NWRs Comprehensive Conservation Plan (2010): "established by President Woodrow Wilson on July 1, 1920, through Executive Order 3299"
American Presidency Project: Proclamation 2416, Changing the Names of Certain Federal Wildlife Refuges (July 25, 1940), lists former and new names

review.note: EO 3299, 1920-07-01 (Woodrow Wilson). Former name Caloosahatchee Reservation per Proclamation 2416. No copy of the EO text was located; date and number rest on the CCP.

designationHistory.indexOriginal: The refuge was established by President Woodrow Wilson on July 1, 1920, through Executive Order 3299 as a ". . . preserve and breeding ground for native birds" upon the recommendation of Thomas and Mina Edison.
